description: Create or update one or more workouts for an athlete (a full training week can be created in one call). Workouts with an existing id are updated, others created. Every session except strength and rest needs a `structure` in interval notation — an easy session is one line, "main 45' @ 65%" — and a call with one missing saves nothing and names the sessions. Targets are expressed against the athlete's thresholds, which list_athletes returns. The reply carries `checks`: what the parser made of each structure (a pool set written in minutes, a repeat that is not a whole number of lengths, an amount in the wrong unit) and what the plan audit makes of the days just written (two quality sessions stacked, no easy day, a load jump). Read them — they are the same checks audit_plan runs, and they point at what to fix. They are findings rather than errors: the sessions are saved either way, and a race-simulation week breaks some of them on purpose. Draws a page in the chat — "The plan" — so the figures are on screen: refer to what the page shows rather than retyping it, and spend your words on what it means.

athlete_id.description: May be omitted when you coach exactly one athlete.

description.description: Full session description: warm-up, main intervals with targets (watts / pace / HR zones), cool-down.

duration_min.description: Duration in minutes. Derived from `structure` — only send this for a strength or rest session, which has none.

id.description: Workout id. Omit to create; pass an existing id to update.

planned_tss.description: Planned Training Stress Score. Derived from `structure` — only send this for a strength or rest session, which has none.

sport.description: xcski is cross-country skiing on snow, rollski roller skiing, inlineskate inline skating, row rowing on the water or the erg, skierg the SkiErg, hiit high-intensity and functional fitness (a Hyrox simulation, station circuits, CrossFit; plain lifting is strength); all six are scored on heart rate and take no interval structure.

status.description: Use "proposed" for drafts the coach must approve — invisible to the athlete and outside the load model until accepted.

structure.description:
Required for every sport except strength and rest. The session itself, one block per line or comma — for every sport, not just the bike. duration_min and planned_tss are READ OUT OF THIS and overwritten, so do not also send them. The first line may be the session's name ("VO2 max intervals"); it becomes the title when none is sent. Amounts: 20' or 20min = minutes, 90s = seconds, 4:00 = min:sec, 400m and 5km = distance (m is METRES, never minutes). Targets are a fraction of that sport's threshold and always point the same way — 105% is harder in every sport, meaning 105% of threshold SPEED for run and swim. Also @ 300W, @ 4:00/km, @ 1:35/100m, @ CSS+3, and in any sport a heart rate: @ 140-150bpm, @ 85% LTHR, @ 75% HRmax (needs the athlete's LTHR or max HR; the watch gets a heart-rate target and the session is graded on heart rate). A DASH IS A RANGE to stay inside, in every unit: 88-92%, 290-310W, 3:55-4:05/km, 135-148bpm. A RAMP SAYS ramp: warmup 20' ramp 45-65% starts at 45% and ends at 65% (heart rate never ramps). Write ramp in warm-ups and cool-downs that build or ease, almost never in a rep; for a steady effort ONE value is clearest (@ 3:22/km). Repeats nest: 4x(12' @ 91%, 4' @ 50%); always state the recovery. "20s rest" is stopped rest. In a brick, a line reading just "bike" or "run" switches leg. Unparsable structures are rejected, so read tripeak://guide/interval-notation first. Examples: "warmup 20' ramp 45-65%
4x(12' @ 91%, 4' @ 50%)
cooldown 10' ramp 60-40%" and "warmup 15' ramp 45-65%
6x(4' @ 3:22/km, 2' jog @ 60%)
cooldown 10' ramp 60-40%".

title.description: A few words, as it reads on the calendar. May be left out when the structure opens with the session's name.

name: create_workouts
